claims.text: The two groups show parallel patterns of repeated SSH authentication failures targeting the root account, but they differ in timing and source address.

In Group 150.183.249.110 the failures occur within a six‑second window on July 10 at 16:01–16:01:47, whereas Group 207.243.167.114 spreads its attempts over an eight‑minute span from 07:02:27 to 07:02:55 on July 26.

Both sets involve the same user (root) and identical log formats, yet the first source fires a burst of five failures in quick succession while the second spreads them out with longer intervals between each attempt.
This concentration of rapid failures from 150.183.249.110 is more anomalous because it suggests an automated brute‑force script rather than a human or intermittent scanner.

A plausible root‑cause hypothesis is that 150.183.249.110 is being used by a compromised botnet or credential‑stuffing tool that is aggressively probing the SSH service for the default root login, while 207.243.167.114 may represent a less aggressive or differently configured scanning source.
